bull.b: Growth across several ophthalmic franchises reduces reliance on a single product and demonstrates expanding commercial adoption. Rising prescriptions, prescribers, ordering accounts, and surgical demand can support recurring revenue growth over the next several quarters.

bull.t: High Margins and Improving Cash Generation
bull.b: Very high gross margins provide a favorable foundation for scaling branded ophthalmic products, while positive operating and free cash flow improve liquidity. If sustained, this combination can fund commercial investment and gradually strengthen financial resilience.

New products and broader payer access expand Harrow’s addressable ophthalmic markets and strengthen its platform strategy. TYRVAYA adds a complementary dry-eye therapy, while PBM coverage may improve VEVYE access, prescription conversion, and commercial scale.

bear.t: Elevated Leverage and Thin Equity Cushion
bear.b: Higher leverage and a reduced equity base limit financial flexibility if operating performance weakens. Debt-funded growth increases the importance of sustained cash generation and may constrain future investment, acquisitions, or other capital allocation choices.

Strong gross margins have not yet translated into consistent profitability because operating costs remain elevated and reported losses have widened. Additional commercialization and integration spending could delay durable earnings conversion and pressure cash resources.

Meeting guidance requires a substantial second-half acceleration across product launches, channel normalization, salesforce productivity, and TYRVAYA execution. Reimbursement loss in ASC settings adds a structural access headwind that could limit uptake for IHEEZO.
